location_qualifier: south of Bloody Ridge, left wing of the 2nd Division envelopment
source_locator: R2225: ch. VI (Nasu’s left wing, the 29th Infantry, delivered the 24–25 October assault east of Bloody Ridge); R2228: C25080233000 pp. 24–25 (stamps 0574–0575), 2nd Division order 24 October 11:00, both wings to assault at 17:00 toward the airfield, and the left wing (29th Infantry named) penetrated around 22:30
current_activity: assaulting the southern perimeter with the 29th Infantry
engaged_note: 1st Battalion, 7th Marines, later reinforced by the 3rd Battalion, 164th Infantry (Miller, ch. VI)
notes: Miller, chapter VI: Nasu’s left wing, built on the 29th Infantry, made the only inland assault of the night of 24–25 October, against the 1st Battalion, 7th Marines, east of Bloody Ridge. The claim date is 24 October, as with the existing 29th Infantry row for that night. Confidence 0.5. Confidence is raised from 0.5 to 0.7. The 17th Army operations record (JACAR C25080233000, stamps 0574–0575) independently confirms the 2nd Division inland assault of the night of 24 October, with the 29th Infantry in the left wing, which agrees with Miller, chapter VI (Nasu’s left wing east of Bloody Ridge). The Japanese text describes the assault toward the airfield from the south and does not use the English name Bloody Ridge.

location_qualifier: south of Bloody Ridge, second night
source_locator: R2225: ch. VI (the 16th and 29th Regiments pressed their attacks until daylight on 26 October, and General Nasu was among the dead of the counter-offensive); R2228: C25080233000 p. 28 (stamp 0578), left-wing commander Maj. Gen. Nasu at the front decided on a night assault on the 25th, and part of the 16th Infantry was stopped by wire and the penetration did not succeed by dawn
current_activity: renewing the inland assault on the second night
engaged_note: 164th Infantry and 1st Battalion, 7th Marines (Miller, ch. VI)
notes: Miller, chapter VI: the 16th and 29th Regiments pressed the inland attacks until daylight on 26 October. This claim is the second night (date 25 October). Confidence 0.5. Miller lists General Nasu among the dead of the counter-offensive but does not give the day of death; that day is not invented. Confidence is raised from 0.5 to 0.7. The 17th Army operations record (JACAR C25080233000, stamp 0578) independently names Maj. Gen. Nasu as left-wing commander and confirms that he ordered a night assault on 25 October, which agrees with Miller, chapter VI (the second night of the inland attacks). Miller lists Nasu among the dead of the counter-offensive but does not give the day of death; that day is still not invented.
